name: Barnabas
charge: Selling his land and laying the money at the apostles' feet; a good man, full of the Holy Ghost and of faith
summary: A Levite of Cyprus sold his land and brought the whole price to the apostles, in the same chapter and by the same rule that Ananias and Sapphira broke with theirs. He took Saul in when the disciples were afraid of him, went to find him in Tarsus when Antioch needed a teacher, and was the man Antioch's Gentiles first believed under. The apostles named him: the son of consolation.
offense: Joses, who by the apostles was surnamed Barnabas, (which is, being interpreted, The son of consolation,) a Levite, and of the country of Cyprus, having land, sold it, and brought the money, and laid it at the apostles' feet. But Barnabas took Saul, and brought him to the apostles. When he came to Antioch, and had seen the grace of God, he was glad, and exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they would cleave unto the Lord. For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost and of faith.
judgment: And much people was added unto the Lord. The Holy Ghost said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them. The Spirit's own naming of him for the first mission to the Gentiles is the blessing; the church's naming of him is the other: son of consolation. His gift and Ananias' lie stand a few verses apart so no one can miss the difference.

entries.commentary: As they spake unto the people, the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees came upon them, grieved that they taught the people and preached through Jesus the resurrection from the dead. The Sadducees, Pharisees, elders, and chief priests were the religious leaders of that day, and they are the same religious leaders today: your Creflo Dollars, your TD Jakes, your Joel Osteens, your Gino Jennings, speaking the same things they spoke back then. The Sadducees were the upper class, the wealthy priestly and merchant families, moved by political and economic position. They came under the influence of Hellenism the same way today's pastors come under the influence of Americanism, preaching a prosperity and a political gospel and adopting their own man-made traditions. They were grieved because the teaching pulled the people, the money, and the control away from them. It is jealousy, envy, and the inability to guide the people, the same reason these pastors avoid a real sit-down with someone who actually knows the scriptures. The Sadducees did not even believe in the resurrection, yet they used scriptures they did not believe to try to confound Christ, the same way Christians and five-percenters take our scriptures they reject and use them to try to confound us. -

They laid hands on them and put them in hold unto the next day. The spirit that was on the Pharisees is being activated again, and everyone plays their role again in this lifetime; just as the disciples are back in the truth, the chief priests, Sadducees, and Pharisees are back too, saying the same things they said before. They insist Christ broke the Sabbath even though Peter and Paul testified that Christ did no sin, which shows the same spirit that was on the Pharisees is on the Christian pastors. The work the Sabbath forbids is occupational labor, not healing or picking corn to eat, and their real motive was envy, because the disciples gathered and unified the people and their control and money were being touched. -

Howbeit many of them which heard the word believed, and the number of the men was about five thousand. Many still hear and believe today, and it is mainly black men leaving the dead churches, because the church gives them no purpose, no structure, no discipline, and no position to lead, teaching them to be docile and subservient. This five thousand disproves the Christian claim that the Jews all rejected Christ. He came unto his own, meaning the religious leaders, the builders, the chief priests and rulers whose job was to guide the nation, and only those upper echelons rejected him, while thousands of the people believed and were zealous of the law. -

On the morrow the rulers, elders, and scribes, with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, and Alexander, and the kindred of the high priest, gathered together at Jerusalem. Annas had been high priest around 6 to 15 AD and kept the title even after the Romans ejected him, while Caiaphas, his son-in-law, was the official high priest the year Christ was killed. These were the very persons who procured the death of Christ. Caiaphas prophesied that one man should die for the people, speaking not of himself but from the prophecies he knew in [Isaiah 53](/bible/isaiah/53) and the Psalms. That nation he must die for is Israel, and "not for that nation only" means Christ would also gather the children of God scattered abroad, the twelve tribes, not the Gentiles the Christians claim. -

When they had set them in the midst, they asked by what power or by what name have ye done this, and Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, said unto them, ye rulers of the people and elders of Israel. The conversation is still to Israel, always the Israelites. Being filled with the Holy Ghost did not mean Peter was shaking, sweating, or speaking in tongues; it means he was filled with the wisdom to speak with poise before the rulers. When you are brought before the synagogues, magistrates, and powers, the Holy Ghost teaches you in that same hour what to say, the way brother Abiel spoke eloquently in court and was released. You must be wise as a serpent and harmless as a dove, and the wisdom of God will speak through you. Peter, Paul, John, and Christ all went to the rulers and builders of the people, not to the white church, the mosque, or the temple of Zeus. Our job is to go to the scribes, Sadducees, Pharisees, and religious leaders of our own captivity to reason and win some, not to the same people who raped, robbed, drugged, and miseducated us and would never give up their power. This is why bishop gave the order to go to these Christian pastors. -

If we this day be examined of the good deed done to the impotent man, by what means he is made whole; be it known that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom ye crucified, whom God raised from the dead, this man stands here before you whole. Examine our good deeds the same way: taking brothers off the streets from drug dealing, gang banging, killing, and stealing; taking sisters out of prostitution; putting black households back together; keeping children from being aborted; keeping men out of prison. What did the disciples do wrong but heal the impotent man? Any time there is a good deed the Pharisees still attack, which shows the hardness of our people's hearts. It was never about the nation or the people; it was about their own vainglory, position, power, and authority.

This is the stone which was set at naught of you builders, which is become the head of the corner. It was the builders' job to build and bind the nation, to raise up the tabernacle of David, to bind the brokenhearted, and to feed the flock, but when the stone, Christ, came, jealousy and vainglory arose and they rejected him. The kingdom is therefore taken from them and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits. Christ is a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, because men stumble at his location, his upbringing, his appearance, and his low social class. He came from the same hoods we came from, from your Philadelphias, your Detroits, the south side of Chicago, so the Most High confounds the wise by the foolish and chooses the base and the underdog, the way he chose David, not the Creflo Dollars, the TD Jakes, the Cornel Wests, or the Umar Johnsons who already have a following and would take the glory for themselves. This is how you know God is working with us, taking men called nobody and setting them before princes. Christ is also a sanctuary, a place of refuge and comfort from the world, from crime, hatred, and murder, and he gives our people a purpose, which is what everybody is looking for. Simeon said the child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel, and the "own" that received him not is the fall of the scribes, Sadducees, and chief priests. -

Neither is there salvation in any other, for there is none other name under heaven given among men whereby we must be saved. Christians reduce this to saying the words "in the name of Jesus," but "none other name" means no other power or authority was given to any man; that authority was given to Christ alone, so there is no salvation in Moses or Elias, only through Christ. You cannot sneak into the kingdom through Islam, the Nation of Islam, Jehovah's Witnesses, Mormonism, Pentecostalism, Seventh-day Adventism, the Baptists, or Buddhism. Whoever climbs up some other way is a thief and a robber trying to sneak in without laboring; you must enter by the door, which is Christ. -

When they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled and took knowledge of them that they had been with Jesus. The rulers saw these men were not slick, cunning, and crafty like themselves; they were bold, coming as if straight off a plantation and a field, not the regular church men. That boldness is the natural animation of the Holy Spirit, not something you force or make up. Brothers who teach weak, like the Christian pastors, with no power and no conviction, are lacking the Holy Spirit. You cannot push the spirit out; when you keep the Most High's laws and stay in the scriptures, the spirit animates your teaching with boldness, the way Christ taught with authority and not as the scribes. People who call us hostile have simply never seen a man of God speak with the Holy Spirit. Peter was fearless and intrepid, a man who drew a sword and cut off the man's ear, which was not the first time he used it; he came from the streets, and we have brothers with that same posture. They took knowledge the disciples had been with Christ because you take on the attributes and characteristics of whoever you surround yourself with, and the disciples all spoke the same thing as Christ. -
Beholding the man which was healed standing with them, they could say nothing against it. The living proof of the miracle was standing right there, and the rulers had no answer.

They commanded them to go aside out of the council and conferred, saying what shall we do to these men, for a notable miracle has been done by them and we cannot deny it; but that it spread no further among the people, let us straitly threaten them and command them not to speak in the name of Jesus. It was never about the miracle but about losing their power and their seat of authority, and you have to be that wicked to witness the great works and still plot against the men who did them. Satan cannot cast out Satan, so they knew the miracle was of the Most High; yet the same way they consulted to put Lazarus back to death after Christ raised him, they chose to threaten the disciples rather than glorify God. That level of hatred, envy, and emulation is what the religious leaders had for the people. The Pharisees were divided over Christ, some saying he is not of God because he healed on the Sabbath, others asking how a man that is a sinner could do such miracles. That same division will bring people out of the Christian church to examine the matter and repent based on our works. -

Peter and John answered, whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye, for we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard. Having further threatened them, the council let them go, finding nothing how they might punish them because of the people, for all men glorified God for the man who was healed, who was above forty years old.

Being let go, they went to their own company and reported all, and they lifted up their voice to God with one accord: Lord, thou art God who made heaven and earth; why did the heathen rage and the people imagine vain things; the kings of the earth stood up and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ. Against the holy child Jesus, Herod, Pontius Pilate, the Gentiles, and the people of Israel were gathered together, and this same thing is going to happen all over again. Their prayer was for boldness to speak the word and that signs and wonders be done, so if you lack the Holy Spirit, your prayer should be that the Most High put it in you, for he gives it freely. When they had prayed, the place was shaken, they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness. -

The multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul, and neither said any of them that ought he possessed was his own, but they had all things common. They did not cleave to materialistic things; when you come into the truth those things lose their importance and your objective becomes how you can support the truth. This is the establishment of a community, for community comes from common. With great power the apostles gave witness of the resurrection, and great grace was upon them all; neither was there any that lacked, for as many as owned lands or houses sold them and laid the money at the apostles' feet, and distribution was made to every man according as he had need. This was not a prosperity doctrine where you give to get rich; you give so that when one lacks, all supply his need, whether food, an eviction, or a proper burial. The church was the epicenter and hub of the community, and the arms, not tithes, circled through it and were distributed according to each man's need. Joseph, surnamed Barnabas, a Levite of Cyprus, sold his land and laid the money at the apostles' feet; this is the same Barnabas who later traveled with Paul, and even as an apostle he gave arms. Every ranked man should give arms as a testament of his faith and leadership, even while spending his own money to travel and teach. --- Topics: [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Saul is still breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples, going to the high priest for letters to Damascus so he can bind any of "this way," whether men or women, and drag them bound to Jerusalem. This is why we tell brothers and sisters both to gird up their minds and build their faith by studying, because when they notice you by your last name or your fringes you will be persecuted. Before the followers of Christ were called Christians in [Acts 11](/bible/acts/11), they were called "this way," meaning the way of Christ. Some people, when the persecution comes, will change their name back, stop wearing fringes, stop keeping the Sabbath, and hide, saying "that's not me." -

As Saul journeys near Damascus a light from heaven, a chariot of the Most High, shines round about him, he falls to the earth, and hears a voice: "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?" Christ was already dead at this time, yet he says "why persecutest thou me," because what you do to one of his little ones you do to him also. Saul did not realize he was in error. He thought the disciples were bringing heresy, but it was not heresy, it was the New Covenant being introduced. Trembling and astonished, he immediately humbles himself and says, "Lord, what wilt thou have me to do."

The men journeying with Saul stood speechless, hearing a voice but seeing no man. People read this against [Acts 22](/bible/acts/22) and claim a contradiction, but there is none. It was a caravan of men. Based on each man's account, one group heard the voice but saw no man, and another group saw the light but heard no voice, just as men running from the same scene report different pieces of it. There is no contradiction in the Bible. -
Saul arose from the earth, and when his eyes were opened he saw no man, so they led him by the hand into Damascus. He was struck blind by what he witnessed. -

Saul is three days without sight, neither eating nor drinking. The Most High speaks in a vision to a disciple at Damascus named Ananias and sends him to the street called Straight, to the house of Judas, to lay hands on Saul. Saul himself is given a vision of Ananias coming to restore his sight. People are still given dreams and visions this way, some seeing a man show them truth before they understood it was about Israel.

Ananias objects: he has heard by many how much evil this man has done to the saints at Jerusalem, and that he holds authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on the Most High's name. Saul had consented to Stephen's death and chased disciples from city to city with zeal. Was Saul doing it in ignorance? Yes. That is why the scripture says judge nothing before the time. The things we all did in the world were worthy of death, so who are we to say a man is beyond repentance? The killer, even a pastor putting us to death in the future, may come to the truth later and say he did it in ignorance, as Christ and Stephen both prayed "Father, forgive them." Even a sister who cursed the teacher out on the streets for months came around and began to listen, because anyone can repent. This is the true meaning of loving your enemies. Christianity twists it to mean love the ones who enslaved, raped, and colonized your ancestors, stole your nationality, land, and heritage, miseducated you, gave you a false image of God, and today shut down anyone who says Israel is the true children of God. That is not the enemy the scripture means. The Bible means love the enemies within your own nation, because Paul, who persecuted and killed the disciples, was one of those enemies who could still repent. -

The Most High tells Ananias to go his way, for Saul is a chosen vessel to bear his name before the Gentiles, kings, and the children of Israel. People discredit Paul's writings, but the book of Acts credits and justifies them, so to throw out Paul you would have to throw out Acts too. The Most High will show Saul how great things he must suffer for his name's sake. The teaching on the Gentiles is held for later, when Paul actually begins his ministry.

Ananias enters, lays his hands on him as "Brother Saul," and immediately something like scales fall from his eyes, he receives sight, and is baptized. Paul was not taught by Peter or the other apostles; Christ himself taught him directly. -

Saul spends certain days with the disciples at Damascus and straightway preaches Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God. Paul constantly has to give his resume, because he came up under Christ, not under the apostles, so the churches needed to know where he came from. -

All who heard were amazed, asking if this is not the same man who destroyed those who called on Christ's name. But Saul increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel; when Christ was revealed, everything started to make sense and he took it to another level. -

After many days the Jews take counsel to kill Saul, watching the gates day and night, so the disciples take him by night and let him down the wall in a basket. This is what you are in: your front door may be occupied and you may have to go down the window on a rope. Properly prepare your mind, because anything can happen at any moment and you must be ready to drop everything and leave. In the world men drove drunk and gang-banged unafraid of death, so do not now be a coward for the truth; the Most High controls death, and it is better to die for this truth than to die for nothing. -

When Saul comes to Jerusalem he tries to join the disciples, but they are afraid of him until Barnabas brings him to the apostles and declares how he had seen the Lord and preached boldly at Damascus. Notice Acts does not tell us he went to Arabia first; Paul fills in that detail himself in Galatians. He goes to Peter and James specifically, the two closest men to Christ, the top apostle and the Lord's brother, so his witness would be established with the leadership. -

Saul speaks boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus and disputes against the Grecians, but they go about to slay him, so the brethren bring him down to Caesarea and send him to Tarsus. Caesarea sits on the coast of Israel bordering the region of Syria near Damascus. -
Then the churches have rest throughout all Judaea, Galilee, and Samaria, are edified, and walking in the fear of the Lord and the comfort of the Holy Ghost, are multiplied. -

As Peter passes through all quarters he comes to the saints at Lydda and finds Aeneas, who had kept his bed eight years sick of the palsy. Peter says, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ maketh thee whole; arise and make thy bed," and he arises immediately. All that dwelt at Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.

At Joppa a disciple named Tabitha, called Dorcas, full of good works and almsdeeds, falls sick and dies, and they wash her and lay her in an upper chamber. Women were disciples too, students and followers of Christ, and washing the dead shows our own customs of purifying the body. The disciples send for Peter, who puts them all out, kneels, prays, and says, "Tabitha, arise." She opens her eyes and sits up, and he presents her alive to the saints and widows, so that many in Joppa believed. Peter then tarries many days in Joppa with Simon a tanner. Dorcas made coats and garments and gave almsdeeds, so she had a good name and no covetous spirit; what she took in she gave back. This is unlike the opportunists who see thousands at Passover and only think of what they can get from the people, coveting to live off of them. --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

The apostles and brethren in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God, and now Peter is rehearsing what happened in [Acts 10](/bible/acts/10). The "Gentiles" is a reference to Cornelius, who was not Italian by nation; he was an Israelite who served as a general over a hundred men in the Roman army, just as today there are black generals and black soldiers in the American army, and America is an extension of ancient Rome. -

When Peter came up to Jerusalem, they of the circumcision contended with him, saying he went in to men uncircumcised and did eat with them. The complaint was about Peter dealing with the Gentiles, meaning the northern kingdom, and there had been contention between the northern and southern kingdom ever since the split under Solomon. To understand circumcision and uncircumcision you have to go to the origin: circumcision was the token, the sign, the seal of the covenant the Most High made with Abraham, a visible confirmation carried through all the generations. -

Peter rehearses the vision from the beginning: he was in Joppa praying, and in a trance saw a vessel descend like a great sheet. That vessel is Israel, swallowed up and consumed among the Gentiles, made a vessel of no honour by learning their works and serving their idols. -

The voice said, "Arise, Peter; slay and eat," but Peter refused because nothing common or unclean had ever entered his mouth. The voice answered, "What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common," because it was never about food but about people. -

Peter continues the account: immediately three men came to the house from Caesarea, and the Spirit bade him go with them, nothing doubting. Six brethren went with him into the man's house, and Cornelius told how an angel had stood in his house and directed him to send to Joppa for Simon Peter, who would tell him words whereby he and all his house would be saved.

As Peter began to speak, the Holy Ghost fell on them as it did on the apostles at the beginning, and Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how that John baptized with water but they would be baptized with the Holy Ghost. Since the Most High gave these Israelites the same gift he gave the apostles who believed on Christ, Peter asks what he was that he could withstand God.

When they heard this they held their peace and glorified God, saying the Most High had also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life. These Gentiles are the Israelites who took on Gentile customs, whether the northern kingdom broken off before Assyria when Pekah the son of Remaliah conspired against Judah, or Judah who became Gentiles under the Greeks. -

Those scattered by the persecution over Stephen traveled as far as Phenice, Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but the Jews only, going where the Israelites were scattered. Phenice was the coastal region north of Israel, modern Lebanon; Cyprus is an island in the eastern Mediterranean; and Antioch was a major Roman city in ancient Syria, now Antakya, Turkey. The reason they preached to the Jews only is the prophecy that the Most High saves the tents of Judah first. -

The hand of the Lord was with them and a great number believed and turned to the Lord. The church at Jerusalem sent Barnabas, a good man full of the Holy Ghost and faith, who exhorted them to cleave to the Lord, then went to Tarsus to seek Saul and brought him to Antioch, where for a whole year they taught much people. The disciples were called Christians first in Antioch, and those disciples were Jews. Christians were not all nations or races as men think today; the Greek word Christianos comes from Christos, the anointed one, so a Christian is a kinsman of the Messiah and a follower of Christ, an anointed one. -

In those days prophets came from Jerusalem to Antioch, and one named Agabus signified by the Spirit that there would be a great dearth throughout all the world, which came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar. This famine is historically documented; Elliott's commentary notes the frequent famines of Claudius's reign, and Josephus records a famine affecting Judea and Syria under the procurator Cuspius Fadus around AD 45, when Queen Helena of Adiabene sent supplies of corn and figs, again giving validity to the Bible as an accurate history book. The disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief to the brethren in Judea, which they did, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul. That is the end of [Acts 11](/bible/acts/11). --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath) ← [Acts 10](/study/acts/10) · [Acts Study](/study/acts)

At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release: every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it, and shall not exact it of his neighbour or of his brother, because it is called the Lord's release. Of a foreigner thou mayest exact it again, but that which is thine with thy brother thine hand shall release. The seven year release stands on the sabbath of the land already given in [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25).

If thou carefully hearken unto the voice of the Most High to observe all these commandments, thou shalt lend unto many nations but thou shalt not borrow, and thou shalt reign over many nations but they shall not reign over thee. This is the blessing that was to come upon us. Since we broke the commandments of the Most High, the other nations lend to us and we borrow from them; we go to them for loans and everything else.

If there be among you a poor man of one of thy brethren, thou shalt not harden thine heart nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother. It is a commandment to us to help our brothers: open thine hand wide unto him and lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.

Beware that there be not a thought in thy wicked heart saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand, and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother and thou givest him nought; if he cry unto the Lord against thee, it is sin unto thee. Give him surely, and let not thine heart be grieved when thou givest, for because of this thing the Most High shall bless thee in all thy works. Notice that Esau had this Bible, these commandments and these laws, yet worked us to death for over four hundred years, and when they released us we did not go out with anything. They had these laws written before them and did not do them. The poor shall never cease out of the land; Christ said the same, that the poor are always going to be among us. That is why no campaign can fight poverty out of existence: Christ said it will always be among us.

If thy brother, an Hebrew man or an Hebrew woman, be sold unto thee and serve thee six years, then in the seventh year thou shalt let him go free, and thou shalt not let him go away empty. When people say slavery was taking place in Africa among us, it was not slavery like we suffered: it was people among us that fell poor and sold themselves to their brothers, the very case this law and [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25) govern. Thou shalt furnish him liberally out of thy flock, out of thy floor, and out of thy winepress; he must leave blessed, with some of the flock, the corn, and the wine. He cannot go out poor the way he came in; that shows you the Most High is a good God. The reason given is memory: remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt, and the Lord thy God redeemed thee.

If the servant say, I will not go away from thee, because he loveth thee and thine house and is well with thee, then thou shalt take an aul and thrust it through his ear unto the door, and he shall be thy servant for ever; likewise unto thy maidservant. It shall not seem hard unto thee when thou sendest him away free, for he hath been worth a double hired servant to thee in serving thee six years. A double hired servant: reading this makes you think about slavery and how many years they had us. We were double hired servants unto them, and we still serve them even to this day.

All the firstling males of thy herd and of thy flock thou shalt sanctify unto the Most High: thou shalt do no work with the firstling of thy bullock, nor shear the firstling of thy sheep. The firstlings were to do no work at all; they were to be sacrificed to the Most High, and thou shalt eat it before the Lord thy God year by year in the place which the Lord shall choose. If there be any blemish therein, as if it be lame or blind, thou shalt not sacrifice it unto the Lord thy God; thou shalt eat it within thy gates, the unclean and the clean person alike, as the roebuck and as the hart. Only thou shalt not eat the blood thereof; thou shalt pour it upon the ground as water.

verses.text: Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold,
And laid them down at the apostles’ feet: and distribution was made unto every man according as he had need.
And Joses, who by the apostles was surnamed Barnabas, (which is, being interpreted, The son of consolation,) a Levite, and of the country of Cyprus,
Having land, sold it, and brought the money, and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
And when Saul was come to Jerusalem, he assayed to join himself to the disciples: but they were all afraid of him, and believed not that he was a disciple.

But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles, and declared unto them how he had seen the Lord in the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how he had preached boldly at Damascus in the name of Jesus.
Then tidings of these things came unto the ears of the church which was in Jerusalem: and they sent forth Barnabas, that he should go as far as Antioch.
Who, when he came, and had seen the grace of God, was glad, and exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they would cleave unto the Lord.
For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost and of faith: and much people was added unto the Lord.
Then departed Barnabas to Tarsus, for to seek Saul:

And when he had found him, he brought him unto Antioch. And it came to pass, that a whole year they assembled themselves with the church, and taught much people. And the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.

Now there were in the church that was at Antioch certain prophets and teachers; as Barnabas, and Simeon that was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen, which had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
As they ministered to the Lord, and fasted, the Holy Ghost said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.
And when they had fasted and prayed, and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.
It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

If there be among you a poor man of one of thy brethren within any of thy gates in thy land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother:
But thou shalt open thine hand wide unto him, and shalt surely lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.
